# `/skill:parley-code-review`

Review a code change and put the review in front of a person as one parley page. You find the
problems; the reviewer reads them on the diff, comments on any line or finding, and decides what
you fix.

Read `/skill:parley-parley` first. It has the loop (check, serve, listen, reply) and says where `parley.mjs`
is. This skill says what goes on the page.

## Input

The argument names the change. With no argument, review the working tree against `HEAD`.

| Argument | The diff |
| --- | --- |
| none | `git diff HEAD` |
| a branch | `git diff <merge base with main>...<branch>` |
| a range, `a..b` | `git diff a..b` |
| a PR number or URL | use `/skill:parley-pr-review` instead |

Read every changed file in full where the diff alone does not show enough, at the head of the
change (`git show <head>:<path>`; the working tree when there is no argument). Read the tests the
change touches, and the callers of what it changes.

## The review

Look for what a careful reviewer would raise: wrong behaviour, missed cases, broken callers,
missing tests, unsafe input, and code that is much harder to read than it needs to be. A finding
names one problem, at one place, with the reason. Leave out style a formatter or linter would
catch. Report what you checked and found clean in the summary, not as findings.

Give each finding a `severity` from `blocker`, `major`, `minor` and `nit`. Add a `suggestion` when
the fix is short and you are sure of it: the replacement code for the finding's lines.

## The document

Write `docs/parley/review-<short name>.json`. The document `id` is the file name without `.json`. Set the document `repo` to the GitHub remote
and the head commit. `examples/code/review-diff.json` in the parley skill folder shows a whole
`diff` block.

1. A `prose` block: what the change does, in two or three sentences; what you checked; the count of
   findings by severity; and your overall view.
2. A `diff` block with the whole diff, `base` and `head`, `severities` set to `{"minor": "warn"}`
   so minor findings stand out from nits, and the findings, each anchored to its
   `file` and `line`. The line is a new-side line inside a hunk of that file; a problem outside
   every hunk goes in the summary. `node parley.mjs block diff --field findings.<name>` explains
   one field of a finding.
3. A `question` block with one `single` question per blocker or major finding, with options `fix`
   ("Fix"), `other` ("Fix differently: say how in a comment") and `leave` ("Leave it"), and your
   recommendation set. Name the finding's title in the prompt. Minor findings and nits need
   no question; the reviewer comments on the ones they care about.

For a diff over about 3,000 lines, keep the files with findings and name the rest in the summary.

## After the review

Follow the loop in `/skill:parley-parley` until the reviewer gives a verdict. Then fix what they chose and
reply to each finding's thread with what you changed. Do not commit, push or post anything the
reviewer did not ask for.
